constraints_for_future_fit.bounds: predeclare symmetric eta bounds/prior; causal update differences may motivate scale exploration but do not calibrate it
constraints_for_future_fit.selection: freeze candidates from TRAIN-only inference before nuisance fit
constraints_for_future_fit.support: cross-scan repeated support is required for a persistent-effects interpretation; within-scan relative effects can be explored separately with predeclared regularization and Jacobian checks
constraints_for_future_fit.validation: select all hyperparameters within TRAIN then score fixed assignments on reserved rows; no validation/test tuning

identifiability.cfo: retain the per-track constant CFO only; short tracks have weak time-shape information and must not receive independent timing terms
identifiability.gauge: one additive gauge per component: u_s+c and eta_k-c; fix one u_s or impose one weighted zero-sum eta constraint; constraining both families adds a model assumption
identifiability.graph: construct the scan-satellite bipartite graph, identify components, then check the actual profiled Doppler Jacobian rather than inferring full numerical rank from connectivity alone
identifiability.location: hold location fixed during a first epoch-nuisance fit, or impose a predeclared location prior; otherwise geometry-induced Doppler changes confound time shifts
identifiability.single_scan_satellites: relative eta contrasts among satellites in one scan can be identified; a common shift of all eta terms trades with the scan term, and useful precision remains data dependent

proposed_model.measurement: for track i in scan s assigned satellite k, predict Doppler at t_i + u_s + eta_k; retain one per-track constant CFO b_i
proposed_model.satellite_term: eta_k is a bounded along-track/epoch nuisance shared only across scan edges for the same candidate k
proposed_model.scan_term: u_s is one combined scan timing nuisance; do not separately estimate a receiver clock and a scan epoch because they enter the same propagation-time direction

recurrence_conclusion: Only one candidate spans two scans, with 43 of 17,358 duration weights (0.2477%); none spans three. Cross-scan persistent-effect separation has little support, but this does not rule out regularized within-scan satellite contrasts.
